sanskrit: na ca sā vanavāsāya devīṃ kṛtamatiṃ tadā śaknoty upāvartayituṃ kuntīṃ dharmaparāṃ satīm
english: Nor could she turn back that queen, the virtuous Kuntī, devoted to dharma, whose mind was fixed upon dwelling in the forest.

sanskrit: tasyās tu taṃ sthiraṃ jñātvā vyavasāyaṃ kurustriyaḥ nivṛttāṃś ca kuruśreṣṭhān dṛṣṭvā prarurudus tadā
english: When the women of the Kurus understood that her resolve was unshakable, and saw the foremost of the Kurus turning back, they then broke into weeping.

sanskrit: upāvṛtteṣu pārtheṣu sarveṣv antaḥpureṣu ca yayau rājā mahāprājño dhṛtarāṣṭro vanaṃ tadā
english: When the sons of Pṛthā had all turned back, and all the inner apartments too, the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, vast in wisdom, then set forth to the forest.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavā api dīnās te duḥkhaśokaparāyaṇāḥ yānaiḥ strīsahitāḥ sarve puraṃ praviviśus tadā
english: The Pāṇḍavas too, wretched and given over to grief and sorrow, all entered the city in their carriages together with their women.

sanskrit: tad ahṛṣṭam ivākūjaṃ gatotsavam ivābhavat nagaraṃ hāstinapuraṃ sastrīvṛddhakumārakam
english: The city of Hāstinapura, with its women, elders, and children, became as though joyless, without a murmur, as if its festivals had departed.

sanskrit: sarve cāsan nirutsāhāḥ pāṇḍavā jātamanyavaḥ kuntyā hīnāḥ suduḥkhārtā vatsā iva vinākṛtāḥ
english: All the Pāṇḍavas were dispirited, filled with grief, bereft of Kuntī and stricken with deep sorrow, like calves cut off from their mother.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭras tu tenāhnā gatvā sumahad antaram tato bhāgīrathītīre nivāsam akarot prabhuḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, having traveled a very great distance that day, the lord then made his dwelling on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī.

sanskrit: prāduṣkṛtā yathānyāyam agnayo vedapāragaiḥ vyarājanta dvijaśreṣṭhais tatra tatra tapodhanaiḥ prāduṣkṛtāgnir abhavat sa ca vṛddho narādhipaḥ
english: The sacred fires, kindled according to rule by the foremost of the twice-born who had mastered the Vedas and whose wealth was their austerity, blazed there on every side; and that aged lord of men too had his fire kindled.

sanskrit: sa rājāgnīn paryupāsya hutvā ca vidhivat tadā saṃdhyāgataṃ sahasrāṃśum upātiṣṭhata bhārata
english: That king, having attended upon the fires and offered oblations according to rule, then worshipped the thousand-rayed sun as it reached the twilight, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: viduraḥ saṃjayaś caiva rājñaḥ śayyāṃ kuśais tataḥ cakratuḥ kuruvīrasya gāndhāryāś cāvidūrataḥ
english: Then Vidura and Saṃjaya made a bed of kuśa grass for the king, that hero of the Kurus, and another for Gāndhārī close beside him.

sanskrit: gāndhāryāḥ saṃnikarṣe tu niṣasāda kuśeṣv atha yudhiṣṭhirasya jananī kuntī sādhuvrate sthitā
english: And close to Gāndhārī, Kuntī, the mother of Yudhiṣṭhira, steadfast in her holy vow, took her seat upon the kuśa grass.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ saṃśravaṇe cāpi niṣedur vidurādayaḥ yājakāś ca yathoddeśaṃ dvijā ye cānuyāyinaḥ
english: And within their hearing Vidura and the rest sat down, as did the officiating priests, each in his appointed place, and the twice-born who were their attendants.

sanskrit: prādhītadvijamukhyā sā saṃprajvālitapāvakā babhūva teṣāṃ rajanī brāhmīva prītivardhanī
english: With its foremost twice-born reciting the sacred texts and its fires blazing high, that night for them became like the night of Brahman, swelling their joy.

sanskrit: tato rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ kṛtapūrvāhṇikakriyāḥ hutvāgniṃ vidhivat sarve prayayus te yathākramam udaṅmukhā nirīkṣanta upavāsaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Then, when the night had passed and they had performed the morning rites, all of them, having offered oblation to the fire according to rule, set forth in due order, facing northward and gazing ahead, given over to fasting.

sanskrit: sa teṣām atiduḥkho 'bhūn nivāsaḥ prathame 'hani śocatāṃ śocyamānānāṃ paurajānapadair janaiḥ
english: That sojourn on the first day was full of grief for them, as they mourned and were mourned over by the people of the city and the countryside.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato bhāgīrathītīre medhye puṇyajanocite nivāsam akarod rājā vidurasya mate sthitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, abiding by the counsel of Vidura, made his dwelling upon the pure bank of the Bhāgīrathī, a place fit for holy folk.

sanskrit: tatrainaṃ paryupātiṣṭhan brāhmaṇā rāṣṭravāsinaḥ kṣatraviṭśūdrasaṃghāś ca bahavo bharatarṣabha
english: There the brāhmaṇas dwelling in the realm waited upon him, as did many companies of kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto rājā kathābhir abhinandya tān anujajñe saśiṣyān vai vidhivat pratipūjya ca
english: Surrounded by them, the king gladdened them with discourse, and having duly honored them along with their pupils, gave them leave to depart.

sanskrit: sāyāhne sa mahīpālas tato gaṅgām upetya ha cakāra vidhivac chaucaṃ gāndhārī ca yaśasvinī
english: In the evening that protector of the earth went down to the Gaṅgā and performed his ablutions according to rule, as did the illustrious Gāndhārī.

sanskrit: tathaivānye pṛthak sarve tīrtheṣv āplutya bhārata cakruḥ sarvāḥ kriyās tatra puruṣā vidurādayaḥ
english: And so too all the others, each apart, having bathed at the sacred fords, O Bhārata, the men there performed all the rites, Vidura and the rest.

sanskrit: kṛtaśaucaṃ tato vṛddhaṃ śvaśuraṃ kuntibhojajā gāndhārīṃ ca pṛthā rājan gaṅgātīram upānayat
english: Then Pṛthā, the daughter of Kuntibhoja, led her aged father-in-law, his ablutions done, and Gāndhārī too, to the bank of the Gaṅgā, O king.

sanskrit: rājñas tu yājakais tatra kṛto vedīparistaraḥ juhāva tatra vahniṃ sa nṛpatiḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ
english: There the king's officiating priests prepared the spreading of the altar, and that lord of men, true to his pledges, offered oblation into the fire.

sanskrit: tato bhāgīrathītīrāt kurukṣetraṃ jagāma saḥ sānugo nṛpatir vidvān niyataḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ
english: Then from the bank of the Bhāgīrathī he journeyed to Kurukṣetra, that learned king with his followers, restrained and with his senses subdued.

sanskrit: tatrāśramapadaṃ dhīmān abhigamya sa pārthivaḥ āsasādātha rājarṣiḥ śatayūpaṃ manīṣiṇam
english: Reaching there the precinct of a hermitage, that wise prince, the royal sage, then came upon the sagacious Śatayūpa.

sanskrit: sa hi rājā mahān āsīt kekayeṣu paraṃtapaḥ sa putraṃ manujaiśvarye niveśya vanam āviśat
english: For he had been a great king among the Kekayas, a scorcher of foes; having established his son in the sovereignty over men, he had entered the forest.

sanskrit: tenāsau sahito rājā yayau vyāsāśramaṃ tadā tatrainaṃ vidhivad rājan pratyagṛhṇāt kurūdvaham
english: Together with him the king then went to the hermitage of Vyāsa, and there, O king, Vyāsa received with due rite that uplifter of the Kurus.

sanskrit: sa dīkṣāṃ tatra saṃprāpya rājā kauravanandanaḥ śatayūpāśrame tasmin nivāsam akarot tadā
english: Having there received consecration, the king, delight of the Kurus, then made his dwelling in that hermitage of Śatayūpa.

sanskrit: tasmai sarvaṃ vidhiṃ rājan rājācakhyau mahāmatiḥ āraṇyakaṃ mahārāja vyāsasyānumate tadā
english: To him that king of great wisdom, with the sanction of Vyāsa, declared the whole rule of forest life, O great king.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa tapasā rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro mahāmanāḥ yojayām āsa cātmānaṃ tāṃś cāpy anucarāṃs tadā
english: Thus the high-minded king Dhṛtarāṣṭra yoked himself to austerity, and his attendants too along with him.

sanskrit: tathaiva devī gāndhārī valkalājinavāsinī kuntyā saha mahārāja samānavratacāriṇī
english: So too the queen Gāndhārī, clad in bark and deerskin, practiced the same vow together with Kuntī, O great king.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā cakṣuṣā cāpi te nṛpa saṃniyamyendriyagrāmam āsthitāḥ paramaṃ tapaḥ
english: In deed, in mind, in speech, and in sight, O king, restraining the whole host of their senses, they took up the highest austerity.

sanskrit: tvagasthibhūtaḥ pariśuṣkamāṃso; jaṭājinī valkalasaṃvṛtāṅgaḥ sa pārthivas tatra tapaś cacāra; maharṣivat tīvram apetadoṣaḥ
english: Reduced to skin and bone, his flesh withered away, wearing matted locks and deerskin, his limbs wrapped in bark, that prince practiced there his austerity, fierce as a great sage and freed of all fault.

sanskrit: kṣattā ca dharmārthavid agryabuddhiḥ; sasaṃjayas taṃ nṛpatiṃ sadāram upācarad ghoratapo jitātmā; tadā kṛśo valkalacīravāsāḥ
english: And Vidura, knower of dharma and statecraft, of foremost intellect, together with Saṃjaya, waited upon that king and his consort, master of himself, then gaunt with terrible austerity and clad in rags of bark.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tasmin muniśreṣṭhā rājānaṃ draṣṭum abhyayuḥ nāradaḥ parvataś caiva devalaś ca mahātapāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then thither the foremost of sages came to see the king — Nārada, and Parvata, and Devala of mighty austerity,

sanskrit: dvaipāyanaḥ saśiṣyaś ca siddhāś cānye manīṣiṇaḥ śatayūpaś ca rājarṣir vṛddhaḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
english: and Dvaipāyana with his pupils, and other sagacious perfected ones, and the royal sage Śatayūpa, aged and most righteous.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kuntī mahārāja pūjāṃ cakre yathāvidhi te cāpi tutuṣus tasyās tāpasāḥ paricaryayā
english: To them Kuntī rendered honor according to rule, O great king, and those ascetics too were well pleased with her ministrations.

sanskrit: tatra dharmyāḥ kathās tāta cakrus te paramarṣayaḥ ramayanto mahātmānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janādhipam
english: There those supreme sages held discourse upon dharma, my son, delighting the great-souled Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of men.

sanskrit: kathāntare tu kasmiṃś cid devarṣir nāradas tadā kathām imām akathayat sarvapratyakṣadarśivān
english: Then in the course of one of these discourses, the divine sage Nārada, who saw all things with his own eyes, told this tale.

sanskrit: purā prajāpatisamo rājāsīd akutobhayaḥ sahasracitya ity uktaḥ śatayūpapitāmahaḥ
english: Of old there was a king, equal to Prajāpati and dreading nothing, called Sahasracitya, the grandsire of Śatayūpa.

sanskrit: sa putre rājyam āsajya jyeṣṭhe paramadhārmike sahasracityo dharmātmā praviveśa vanaṃ nṛpaḥ
english: Having laid the kingdom upon his eldest son, who was most righteous, that king Sahasracitya, the soul of dharma, entered the forest.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tapasaḥ pāraṃ dīptasya sa narādhipaḥ puraṃdarasya saṃsthānaṃ pratipede mahāmanāḥ
english: Having reached the far shore of blazing austerity, that high-minded lord of men attained the abode of Purandara.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭapūrvaḥ sa bahuśo rājan saṃpatatā mayā mahendrasadane rājā tapasā dagdhakilbiṣaḥ
english: Many a time before, O king, as I flew through the air, I saw that king in the hall of great Indra, his sins burned away by austerity.

sanskrit: tathā śailālayo rājā bhagadattapitāmahaḥ tapobalenaiva nṛpo mahendrasadanaṃ gataḥ
english: So too the king Śailālaya, grandsire of Bhagadatta, by the very might of his austerity went to the hall of great Indra.

sanskrit: tathā pṛṣadhro nāmāsīd rājā vajradharopamaḥ sa cāpi tapasā lebhe nākapṛṣṭham ito nṛpaḥ
english: And there was a king named Pṛṣadhra, the equal of the thunderbolt-bearer; he too by austerity won from this very place the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: asminn araṇye nṛpate māndhātur api cātmajaḥ purukutso nṛpaḥ siddhiṃ mahatīṃ samavāptavān
english: In this very forest, O king, the son of Māndhātṛ, King Purukutsa, attained a great perfection.

sanskrit: bhāryā samabhavad yasya narmadā saritāṃ varā so 'sminn araṇye nṛpatis tapas taptvā divaṃ gataḥ
english: He whose wife was Narmadā, the best of rivers — that king, having practiced austerity in this forest, went to heaven.

sanskrit: śaśalomā ca nāmāsīd rājā paramadhārmikaḥ sa cāpy asmin vane taptvā tapo divam avāptavān
english: And there was a king named Śaśalomā, most righteous; he too, having practiced austerity in this wood, attained heaven.

sanskrit: dvaipāyanaprasādāc ca tvam apīdaṃ tapovanam rājann avāpya duṣprāpāṃ siddhim agryāṃ gamiṣyasi
english: And by the grace of Dvaipāyana, O king, you too, having reached this forest of austerity, shall attain the foremost perfection, hard to win.

sanskrit: tvaṃ cāpi rājaśārdūla tapaso 'nte śriyā vṛtaḥ gāndhārīsahito gantā gatiṃ teṣāṃ mahātmanām
english: You too, O tiger among kings, at the end of your austerity, encompassed by splendor and together with Gāndhārī, shall go to the goal of those great-souled ones.

sanskrit: pāṇḍuḥ smarati nityaṃ ca balahantuḥ samīpataḥ tvāṃ sadaiva mahīpāla sa tvāṃ śreyasi yokṣyati
english: And Pāṇḍu, near the slayer of Bala, ever remembers you, O protector of the earth; he will join you to your highest good.

sanskrit: tava śuśrūṣayā caiva gāndhāryāś ca yaśasvinī bhartuḥ salokatāṃ kuntī gamiṣyati vadhūs tava
english: And by serving you and Gāndhārī, the illustrious Kuntī, your daughter-in-law, shall attain to the same world as her husband.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya jananī sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ vayam etat prapaśyāmo nṛpate divyacakṣuṣā
english: She is the mother of Yudhiṣṭhira, and this is the eternal dharma; we behold it, O king, with our divine sight.

sanskrit: pravekṣyati mahātmānaṃ viduraś ca yudhiṣṭhiram saṃjayas tvadanudhyānāt pūtaḥ svargam avāpsyati
english: And Vidura shall enter into the great-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, while Saṃjaya, purified by his devotion to you, shall attain heaven.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā kauravendro mahātmā; sahaiva patnyā prītimān pratyagṛhṇāt vidvān vākyaṃ nāradasya praśasya; cakre pūjāṃ cātulāṃ nāradāya
english: Hearing this, the great-souled lord of the Kurus, glad together with his wife, received and praised the learned words of Nārada, and rendered unmatched honor to Nārada.

sanskrit: tathā sarve nāradaṃ viprasaṃghāḥ; saṃpūjayām āsur atīva rājan rājñaḥ prītyā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya te vai; punaḥ punaḥ samahṛṣṭās tadānīm
english: So too all the companies of brāhmaṇas honored Nārada exceedingly, O king, and out of love for King Dhṛtarāṣṭra they rejoiced again and again at that time.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca nāradasya tu tad vākyaṃ praśaśaṃsur dvijottamāḥ śatayūpas tu rājarṣir nāradaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: The foremost of the twice-born praised that speech of Nārada, but the royal sage Śatayūpa spoke these words to Nārada:

sanskrit: aho bhagavatā śraddhā kururājasya vardhitā sarvasya ca janasyāsya mama caiva mahādyute
english: Ah, O greatly radiant one, by your reverence the faith of the Kuru king has been increased, and that of all these people, and my own as well.

sanskrit: asti kā cid vivakṣā tu mama tāṃ gadataḥ śṛṇu dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ prati nṛpaṃ devarṣe lokapūjita
english: But there is something I would say; hear it as I speak, concerning King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O divine sage, honored by the world.

sanskrit: sarvavṛttāntatattvajño bhavān divyena cakṣuṣā yuktaḥ paśyasi devarṣe gatīr vai vividhā nṛṇām
english: You know the truth of all that comes to pass, and endowed with divine sight, O divine sage, you behold the manifold destinies of men.

sanskrit: uktavān nṛpatīnāṃ tvaṃ mahendrasya salokatām na tv asya nṛpater lokāḥ kathitās te mahāmune
english: You have told of kings attaining the world of great Indra, but the worlds of this king you have not declared, O great sage.

sanskrit: sthānam asya kṣitipateḥ śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ vibho tvattaḥ kīdṛk kadā veti tan mamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ
english: I wish to hear from you, O mighty one, the abode of this lord of the earth — of what kind it is and when he shall attain it; declare that to me as I ask.

sanskrit: ity ukto nāradas tena vākyaṃ sarvamanonugam vyājahāra satāṃ madhye divyadarśī mahātapāḥ
english: Thus addressed by him, Nārada, the seer of divine vision and of great austerity, uttered in the midst of the good a speech that won every heart.

sanskrit: yadṛcchayā śakrasado gatvā śakraṃ śacīpatim dṛṣṭavān asmi rājarṣe tatra pāṇḍuṃ narādhipam
english: By chance I went to the hall of Śakra and saw Śakra, the lord of Śacī; and there, O royal sage, I beheld Pāṇḍu, the lord of men.

sanskrit: tatreyaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya kathā samabhavan nṛpa tapaso duścarasyāsya yad ayaṃ tapyate nṛpaḥ
english: There this very talk of Dhṛtarāṣṭra arose, O king — of this hard austerity that the king is now practicing.

sanskrit: tatrāham idam aśrauṣaṃ śakrasya vadato nṛpa varṣāṇi trīṇi śiṣṭāni rājño 'sya paramāyuṣaḥ
english: There I heard this from the mouth of Śakra, O king: that three years remain of this king's full span of life.

sanskrit: tataḥ kuberabhavanaṃ gāndhārīsahito nṛpaḥ vihartā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'yaṃ rājarājābhipūjitaḥ
english: Thereafter this king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with Gāndhārī, honored by the king of kings, shall roam at will in the dwelling of Kubera,

sanskrit: kāmagena vimānena divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ ṛṣiputro mahābhāgas tapasā dagdhakilbiṣaḥ
english: in a celestial car moving at his will, adorned with divine ornaments — that son of a sage, blessed and great, his sins burned away by austerity.

sanskrit: saṃcariṣyati lokāṃś ca devagandharvarakṣasām svacchandeneti dharmātmā yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: And that soul of dharma shall range freely through the worlds of gods, gandharvas, and rākṣasas — this is the answer to what you ask of me.

sanskrit: devaguhyam idaṃ prītyā mayā vaḥ kathitaṃ mahat bhavanto hi śrutadhanās tapasā dagdhakilbiṣāḥ
english: This great secret of the gods I have told you out of affection; for you, whose wealth is sacred learning, have had your sins burned away by austerity.

sanskrit: iti te tasya tac chrutvā devarṣer madhuraṃ vacaḥ sarve sumanasaḥ prītā babhūvuḥ sa ca pārthivaḥ
english: Hearing that sweet speech of the divine sage, all of them, glad at heart, became delighted, and so did the prince.

sanskrit: evaṃ kathābhir anvāsya dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇaḥ viprajagmur yathākāmaṃ te siddhagatim āsthitāḥ
english: Having thus attended upon Dhṛtarāṣṭra with their discourses, those sages departed each as he wished, taking the path of the perfected ones.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vanaṃ gate kauravendre duḥkhaśokasamāhatāḥ babhūvuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan mātṛśokena cārditāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the lord of the Kurus had gone to the forest, the Pāṇḍavas were overcome with grief and sorrow, O king, and tormented by mourning for their mother.

sanskrit: tathā paurajanaḥ sarvaḥ śocann āste janādhipam kurvāṇāś ca kathās tatra brāhmaṇā nṛpatiṃ prati
english: So too all the townsfolk remained mourning for the lord of men, and there the brāhmaṇas held discourse concerning the king:

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu rājā vṛddhaḥ sa vane vasati nirjane gāndhārī ca mahābhāgā sā ca kuntī pṛthā katham
english: How does that aged king dwell in the lonely forest, and the blessed Gāndhārī, and how fares Kuntī, the daughter of Pṛthā?

sanskrit: sukhārhaḥ sa hi rājarṣir na sukhaṃ tan mahāvanam kimavasthaḥ samāsādya prajñācakṣur hatātmajaḥ
english: That royal sage deserves comfort, yet that great forest is no place of comfort; in what state does he abide, having reached it — he whose eye is wisdom and whose sons are slain?

sanskrit: suduṣkaraṃ kṛtavatī kuntī putrān apaśyatī rājyaśriyaṃ parityajya vanavāsam arocayat
english: A most difficult thing has Kuntī done: not looking upon her sons, she forsook the splendor of the kingdom and chose to dwell in the forest.

sanskrit: viduraḥ kimavasthaś ca bhrātuḥ śuśrūṣur ātmavān sa ca gāvalgaṇir dhīmān bhartṛpiṇḍānupālakaḥ
english: And in what state is Vidura, self-possessed, serving his brother, and the wise son of Gavalgaṇa, Saṃjaya, who cherishes the sustenance given by his master?

sanskrit: ākumāraṃ ca paurās te cintāśokasamāhatāḥ tatra tatra kathāś cakruḥ samāsādya parasparam
english: And the townsfolk, down to the very children, struck by anxiety and grief, held such talk here and there, meeting one another.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś caiva te sarve bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇāḥ śocanto mātaraṃ vṛddhām ūṣur nāticiraṃ pure
english: And all the Pāṇḍavas too, deeply given over to grief, mourning their aged mother, dwelt in the city but a little while.

sanskrit: tathaiva pitaraṃ vṛddhaṃ hataputraṃ janeśvaram gāndhārīṃ ca mahābhāgāṃ viduraṃ ca mahāmatim
english: And likewise grieving for their aged father, the lord of men whose sons were slain, and for the blessed Gāndhārī, and for Vidura of great wisdom.
